title: Noise triage layers, synthetic canaries, and autoresolve playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: We continue to receive noisy paging for transient region-level SLO blips caused by downstream cache thrashing and bursty KV-cache misses during heavy prefix patterns. On-call teams are burning cycles on alerts that resolve before human intervention, which lengthens meantime-to-ack and reduces trust in pager signals. Goal: Implement a multi-layer triage and mitigation system that (1) reduces human pages for high-noise signals, (2) surfaces high-confidence incidents requiring immediate action, and (3) automates safe short-term remediation (autoscale, circuit-breaker triggered load-shed, and synthetic canary reruns) with an autoresolve path when automated fixes succeed. This ticket covers the design and delivery of the alerting rules, synthetic canaries, runbook updates, and playbook automation for the primary production region and the multi-region failover path.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for transient SLO Blip alerts reduces by >=50% during non-incident traffic spikes (measured over 14-day window)
Critical incidents still page immediately and have clear high-confidence predicates that bypass suppression
Automated mitigation (circuit breaker to load-shed + controlled model fallback) executes without human approval for targeted low-impact classes and successfully remediates >=70% of matched events
Synthetic canary suite reruns within 30s of an alert and flags regressions to a separate critical channel
Updated on-call runbooks documented with step-by-step playflows, and a napkin runbook for SRE-on-call
Post-rollout measurement dashboard (tokens-per-request, tail latency P99, page counts) published and linked in ticket
implementation_notes: Step 1: Introduce two-tier alerting predicates: (A) noisy-suppression layer for low-confidence bursts using temporal hysteresis and correlated signal gating, (B) high-confidence layer that bypasses suppression and pages immediately

Step 2: Add short-lived auto-remediation actions: enable internal circuit-breaker to shed best-effort traffic class, scale a reserved node pool by +20% via autoscale API, and route a subset of traffic to model-variant fallback (quantized variant)
Step 3: Implement synthetic canaries: lightweight probe requests that mirror common prefix patterns; execute in region and cross-region; compare response latency and perplexity delta against baseline
Step 4: Implement autoresolve: remediation runs validation via synthetic canaries; if canaries pass for 2 consecutive runs (30s apart) then system auto-resolves alert and records evidence
Step 5: Update runbooks: add decision-tree for when to escalate to on-call, how to manually trigger circuit-breaker off/on, and post-incident remediation steps
Step 6: Safe rollout: start in staging, then 10% of traffic in canary region, then regional gradual rollout with rollback gates based on canary metrics
Notes: Must avoid mask-and-forget: every suppressed alert must create a hidden ticket/record with metadata to enable later analysis and SLG audits
rollout_plan: Week 1: Design review with PM/Design/SRE, finalize alert predicates and canary payloads (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/ENG-84671+Noise+Triage+Design)
Week 2: Implement alert rule changes and synthetic canaries in staging; instrument new metrics (suppressed_count, auto_remediation_count, canary_pass_rate)
Week 3: Run 2-week dark launch in prod (suppression active but pages only to #alerts-suppressed channel), collect baseline
Week 4: Enable autoresolve for low-impact classes in a single region (us-west-1) behind feature flag; monitor for 72 hours
Week 5: Expand autoscale/autorem remediation cross-region and enable low-volume traffic routing to fallback models; follow with incident simulation
Final: Full rollout with dashboard and runbook training for on-call teams
